Demonstrating highest ethical principles conducting Local law, our company’s Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and regulations. Your Profile: 3-5 years of pharmaceutical or biotech sales experience, ideally in specialty care. Experience in Pulmonary Hypertension, Intestinal Lung Disease or Rare Diseases is a strong plus. Degree in Life Sciences, medical/paramedical field or another relevant discipline with healthcare curriculum from an accredited institution. shqa Certification «Certified Pharma Sales Representative» is a strong plus. Proven experience in managing an existing product portfolio and successfully launching a new product. Strong track record of achieving sales targets and supporting marketing efforts in a complex medical environment. Excellent communication, relationship-building and presentation skills. Ability to manage multiple priorities, with strong organizational and strategic planning skills. Experience collaborating with marketing teams to create and implement marketing materials, campaigns and projects. Open to innovation and experimentation. Fluent in German and additionally English. Adaptable to change, ambiguity and a high level of resilience in the face of challenges. Independent, motivated and highly organized. Excellent interpersonal skills in communication, persuasion and customer relations. Possessing a strong learning mindset. Identification of challenges or obstacles and proactively ideate on solutions. Data-driven decision-making and mindset. Comfortable with commercial experimentation and implementing customer projects. title: Senior Pharmaceutical Specialist
description: Job Description Wil jij met jouw expertise bijdragen aan een gezondere wereld? Binnen ons innovatieve team in Haarlem zorg je samen met collega’s voor de veilige distributie van geneesmiddelen en vaccins naar meer dan 140 landen. Voor ons Global Logistics team in Haarlem zoeken we een: Senior Pharmaceutical Specialist. Ben je enthousiast over kwaliteit, samenwerking en continue verbetering? Dan maken we graag kennis met je. Welkom in ons team Vanuit onze locatie in Haarlem distribueren we 2.500 verschillende verpakkingen van geneesmiddelen en vaccins naar meer dan 140 landen. Onze site bestaat uit meerdere productieafdelingen (Integrated Proces Teams - IPT) en Centers of Excellence. IPT Global Logistics verbindt deze afdelingen met elkaar en werkt nauw samen met zowel interne klanten: verpakkings- en productieafdelingen, als externe klanten: supply chain- en / distributiecentra. Binnen Global Logistics werken we aan een compliant, efficiënt en betrouwbaar logistiek proces. Hierbij zijn de teams verantwoordelijk voor de deelprocessen inbound, sample name, dispensing, pick/pack, opslag en outbound nauwkeurig op elkaar ingespeeld. Deze werkzaamheden vinden plaats in zowel een cold store als een ambient warehouse. Je werkt samen met ongeveer 90 collega’s die vanuit verschillende rollen bijdragen aan een optimale en toekomstbestendige logistieke supply chain. Wij zijn op zoek naar een Senior Pharmaceutical Specialist Team Lead die energie krijgt van kwaliteit, team coaching en het verbeteren van processen op kwaliteitsgebied. Het huidige PS-team bestaat uit 2 Pharmaceutical Specialisten en 1 Associate Specialist Quality Assurance. Je zult deel uit maken van en coaching geven aan een betrokken team waarin kennisdeling, zorgvuldigheid en elkaar helpen centraal staan. Over de functie Als Senior Pharmaceutical Specialist speel je een belangrijke rol in het borgen van GMP (Good Manufacturing Practice) en GDP (Good Distribution Practice) binnen de afdeling. Je helpt collega’s om kwaliteit zichtbaar, begrijpelijk en toepasbaar te maken in het dagelijkse werk en bent de GMP/GDP-vraagbaak voor al je collega’s. Je bent medeverantwoordelijk voor de kwaliteit van het proces van ontvangst, opslag en verzending van geneesmiddelen en vaccins. Bij kwaliteitsafwijkingen ben je het aanspreekpunt voor collega’s. Je beoordeelt de ernst en impact, stemt af met de kwaliteitsafdeling en adviseert de Manager Operations over de voortzetting van het proces en de geschiktheid van batches of verpakkingen voor de markt. Samen met je collega’s voer je de GMP-strategie voor de afdeling uit en controleer je of het logistieke proces aan alle wet- en regelgeving voldoet. Je werkt aan klachtafhandeling, deviatiemanagement, change control, quality risk management en temperatuurexcursies. Ook speel je een rol in het opstellen van (kwalificatie)documenten en het voorbereiden van jaarlijkse reviews. Verder vertegenwoordig je de afdeling bij in- en externe audits. Je draagt actief bij aan kwaliteitsverbeteringen binnen het IPT. Je rapporteert aan de IPT Lead Global Logistics. Primaire verantwoordelijkheden Je adviseert over het effect van veranderingen en afwijkingen in het operationele proces op de kwaliteit van het eindproduct. Je vertaalt externe richtlijnen naar praktisch toepasbaar farmaceutisch beleid en duidelijke procedures. Je beoordeelt afwijkingen op procedures en beleidslijnen, autoriseert GMP-documentatie en adviseert bij GMP-inspecties. Je onderzoekt samen met teamleden complexe of hoge-impact kwaliteitsissues en gebruikt trendanalyses om oorzaken en verbetermogelijkheden te vinden. Je ondersteunt de logistieke afdeling bij correctieve en preventieve maatregelen (CAPA’s) naar aanleiding van geconstateerde afwijkingen. Je voert Quality Risk Assessments uit en faciliteert gesprekken waarin verschillende perspectieven worden meegenomen. Je draagt bij aan de kwaliteit van het IPT door verbeteringen te initiëren, voortgang te monitoren en samen prioriteiten te stellen. Je denkt mee over de strategie voor validatie en protocollen en helpt bij de uitvoering hiervan. Jouw profiel Je hebt een afgeronde HBO- of WO-opleiding in een relevant studiegebied, bijvoorbeeld farmacie, life sciences, kwaliteit, logistiek of een vergelijkbare richting. Je brengt bij voorkeur 3-5 jaar ervaring mee met farmaceutisch-technische aspecten, GMP-processen en/of Packaging Technology. Ervaring met GDP is een pré; je krijgt daarnaast ruimte om je verder te ontwikkelen in de rol. Je neemt initiatief, werkt zorgvuldig en kunt keuzes maken wanneer je met kwaliteitsdilemma’s te maken krijgt. Je voelt je prettig in een dynamische logistieke omgeving en kunt goed schakelen wanneer prioriteiten veranderen. Je communiceert helder en respectvol in het Nederlands en Engels en werkt graag samen met collega’s uit verschillende disciplines. Wij bieden Werken bij onze organisatie betekent samen werken aan gezondheid in een internationale werkomgeving met toegewijde collega’s. Je krijgt alle ruimte om jezelf te ontwikkelen en te laten zien wie jij bent. Verder kan je rekenen op aantrekkelijke arbeidsvoorwaarden: Een marktconform salaris, afhankelijk van jouw kennis en ervaring. Een eindejaarsuitkering van 3% en een jaarlijkse bonus op basis van individuele en bedrijfsresultaten. Minimaal 35,5 vakantiedagen. Reiskostenvergoeding en een solide pensioenregeling. Een hoogwaardig bedrijfsrestaurant met dagelijks verse en gezonde opties. Gym en sportveld op de campus. Ondersteuning voor mentaal welzijn via Lyra Health, voor jou en je gezinsleden. Toegang tot een speciale gebeds- en meditatieruimte. Ruime mogelijkheden voor loopbaangroei dankzij de omvang van de locatie en de aanwezigheid van veel disciplines en wereldwijde afdelingen in Boxmeer. Een werkplek binnen een organisatie die blijft groeien en zich blijft ontwikkelen. Twijfel je of je aan alle functie-eisen voldoet? We moedigen je aan om toch te solliciteren. We vinden motivatie, leervermogen en samenwerking belangrijk en kijken graag samen naar wat jij meebrengt. description: Job Description We zijn op zoek naar een gemotiveerde student in het derde jaar of vierde jaar van de opleiding microbiologie/biochemie/procestechnologie ! Wil je graag weten hoe het is om deel uit te maken van een van de grootste multinationale bedrijven in de farmaceutische industrie? We bieden een stageplaats binnen onze afdeling Tissue Culture Boxmeer (TCB) waar je vrijheid en ruimte krijgt voor eigen initiatief. Stagiair - MBO M ic robiologie/Biochemie/Procestechnologie - Tissue Culture Boxmeer Welkom bij ons team De afdeling TCB is een essentiële spil in onze organisatie. Deze afdeling is gericht op op de productie van voornamelijk virale antigenen in rollerbottles en single use bioreactoren. Het team werkt nauw samen met andere afdelingen binnen het bedrijf om de gestelde doelen te bereiken. Je hoofdtaak bestaat uit het zelfstandig en accuraat uitvoeren van de meest voorkomende werkzaamheden, welke nodig zijn om de antigenen te produceren. Werkt volgens een gedetailleerde dagplanningen, houdt toezicht op de kwaliteit, herkent afwijkingen en meld deze tijdig. Jouw stageopdracht Als stagiair ben je verantwoordelijk voor: Bereiden van media, welke gebruikt worden bij het opkweken van cellen en virussen en het inactiveren. Produceren van virale antigenen en controleren van biologische kweekprocessen in roller bottles en bioreactoren. Signaleren van afwijkingen en storingen m.b.t. proces, apparatuur en veiligheid Kan worden ingezet op de meest voorkomende USP en DSP stappen binnen de afdeling (USP: celopstart, celpassage, infectie, ,zowel in rollerbottle als in bioreactor. DSP diverse methodes van virus oogst, sonificeren, inactiveren, concentreren en zuiveringstechnieken). Assisteren en ondersteunen bij probleemanalyses van grondstof tot eindproduct en het oplossen hiervan, daarbij gebruik makende van MPS technieken zoals Scientific Problem Solving of Kaizen. De beschreven werkzaamheden vormen het basispakket en zullen na een goede inwerk- en leerperiode vaak zelfstandig uitgevoerd worden. Op eigen initiatief of door vraag vanuit de organisatie kunnen deze worden aangevuld met andere projecten en/of taken. Wat is vereist Een derdejaars of vierdejaars BOL-3 of 4 student microbiologie, biochemie en procestechnologie die: 4 of 5 dagen per week gedurende een periode van 5 tot 9 maanden beschikbaar is. Een professionele houding heeft, enthousiasme en leergierigheid met zich meebrengt en het een uitdaging vindt om in een dynamische complexe omgeving stage te lopen. Your role is to ensure that our ServiceNow investments deliver scalable, intuitive, and highly efficient digital workflows that support our global operations and mission to save and improve lives. Monitor industry trends and upcoming ServiceNow release features to recommend continuous improvement initiatives. Testing, Quality Assurance & UAT Define testing strategies and compile comprehensive test scenarios to validate that developed features meet all defined acceptance criteria. Facilitate and oversee User Acceptance Testing (UAT) with business stakeholders, acting as the first line of triage for defects and functional feedback. Ensure all development artifacts and system changes are thoroughly documented for future reference and compliance audits. Enablement, Adoption & Change Management Create, maintain , and publish user guides, knowledge articles, and training materials to support successful platform adoption. title: Associate Principal Scientist, Combination Product Design Verification (Associate Director Equivalent)
description: Job Description Job Description Are you enthusiastic and driven to create and lead execution of combination product testing strategies for innovative combination products? Join our company’s Device Development & Technology (DD&T) Team, which focuses on the design, development, and commercialization of novel biologic/drug/vaccine-device combination products for safe and effective delivery to their intended sites of action. The DD&T Team oversees the development of the device constituent within our pipeline of combination products, spanning various therapeutic areas and routes of administration, including inhalation, implantation, and injection. The Associate Principal Scientist will provide end‑to‑end technical and project leadership for the definition, integration, and execution of comprehensive testing strategies in support of the overall control strategy for drug–device combination products. This role has a primary focus on design verification while encompassing the full spectrum of testing activities, including test method development and validation, analytical transfers, incoming testing, in-process, release testing, and testing readiness to enable successful clinical introduction and commercialization. This position plays a critical leadership role across the product lifecycle, partnering with cross‑functional teams and suppliers to ensure testing strategies are aligned with development, manufacturing, regulatory, and quality objectives. In addition to design verification, the Associate Principal Scientist will contribute to and support key validation activities such as drug product manufacturing processes and combination product final assembly process validations, ensuring robust and compliant execution from development through commercial launch. As a matrixed project leader, the incumbent will collaborate extensively with stakeholders within and outside of Device Development & Technology, effectively coordinating teams, timelines, and deliverables to drive testing strategy implementation and execution. Success in this role requires the ability to engage and influence at all organizational levels, translating technical requirements into executable plans that support clinical readiness, regulatory submissions, and market approvals. The role requires deep technical expertise across drug and device development, including design controls, risk management, manufacturing process development and validation, materials, molding technologies, design verification, and design validation. Leveraging this foundation, the Associate Principal Scientist will develop and execute integrated testing strategies that ensure product quality, compliance, and readiness throughout the end‑to‑end development and commercialization lifecycle of combination products. Principal Responsibilities Lead, set direction, align with key stakeholders, and successfully execute, design verification strategies for assigned drug-device combination product program(s) for successful clinical introduction(s) and commercial market(s) approval(s). Define design input(s)/ output(s) and lead associated combination product design verification plan, protocol(s), and report(s) that demonstrate design output(s) meet design input(s). Lead establishment of test methodologies, including method development and validation, internally or externally, per design verification strategy. Lead strategy and execution of accelerated and real time aging studies including bridging studies at the device component/ subassembly/ in-process material and combination product level. Lead stablishing test methodologies/ testing readiness and execution in support of critical activities such as stability studies, drug product filling process validation, combination product final assembly process validation, shipping studies, etc. Support establishment of incoming and release tests at the component and combination product level with key functional areas. Oversee design verification activities performed by external partners. Proactively anticipate and resolve project obstacles and effectively communicate complex product technical challenges, design verification strategy, timelines, milestones, and risks within our Company and with external partners. Author and review relevant portions of the regulatory submissions (INDs, IMPDs, NDAs, BLAs, etc.) for combination product programs under your leadership. Lead/ Support clinical supplies production with respect to device component and combination product testing. Maintain a high level of engagement with cross-functional team members to effectively implement and successfully execute against design verification strategies. Stay current with new device technologies, relevant worldwide regulations, standards, and effectively share this knowledge with others. Enhance our Company’s professional image and competitive advantage through publications, presentations, patents, and professional activities. Qualifications Requirements: B.S. in Mechanical Engineering (or an equivalent field) + 8 years of combination product development experience; M.S. in Mechanical Engineering (or an equivalent field) + 5 years of combination product development experience; or a Ph.D. in Mechanical Engineering (or an equivalent field) + 3 years of combination product development experience. Leadership experience of combination product design verification programs and leading activities (e.g., strategy/ plan, protocol(s), report(s), test method development/validation, etc.) requiring cross-disciplinary project teams. Leadership experience with comprehensive knowledge of various aspects of device development and their interdependencies with design verification, including but not limited to, design controls, risk management, materials & molding, process development and validation, secondary packaging development & qualification, and design validation. Comprehensive understanding of drug product development in addition to device development expertise. Strong familiarity with regulatory landscape associated with drug delivery combination product and design verification requirements. Strong working knowledge of standards relevant to device components and combination products, including ISO 11608, ISO 11040, ISO 80369, as well as performance tests related to container closure integrity and dose accuracy, among others. Proven track record of applying analytical skills in product test method design, development, and validation. Working knowledge of analytical test method technology transfer process. Skilled in laboratory good documentation practices and electronic documentation systems. Self-motivated with ability to work independently. Proven ability to lead teams across multiple disciplines and backgrounds. Strong interpersonal skills and a strategic thinker; able to influence without formal authority; ability to influence and present ideas to senior leadership. Excellent communication, prioritization, presentation, negotiation, project management, and organizational skills. Preferred experiences include: Combination product drug delivery device components – plastic, metal, glass, elastomeric materials, etc. – fracture, stress-strain response, friction, hardness, surface roughness, surface energy quantification. Combination product sub-assemblies (including electro-mechanical) – system tear down analysis, gear ratio optimization, weakest link component identification and optimization, etc. Material characterization and failure mode analysis and integration with combination product risk management. Stress-strain testing of different materials under different environmental conditions, i.e., temperature, humidity. Eagerness to identify lab capability gaps, drive procurement of new equipment, and quickly upskill (also train others) on operation. Experience with analytical or numerical simulation. Excellent collaboration and ideation skills, including facilitating brainstorming sessions, developing proof of concepts, and generating feasibility data. Strong familiarity with compression/tensile testing (Instron, Zwick, Texture Analyzer), rheology (TA Instrument), metrology/non-destructive inspection (XRCT [Zeiss], Optical microscopy [Keyence], high speed imaging) Experience in 3D CAD (Solidworks) and rapid manufacturing techniques (machining, 3D printing) for fixture development and device redesign efforts. description: Job Description Position Overview Translational Molecular Biomarkers (TMB) develops, validates, and deploys biomarker assays across all therapeutic areas and stages of clinical development to enable pipeline decision-making. TMB laboratories translate biomarker strategies into fit-for-purpose clinical assays that inform target engagement, mechanism of action, patient selection, pharmacodynamic response, and clinical outcomes. The Molecular Pathology Laboratory Lead is a senior scientific and people leader responsible for the strategic direction and operations of the Molecular Pathology laboratory. The successful candidate will lead a team of laboratory-based scientists developing, validating, transferring, and deploying tissue-based biomarker assays in support of our Company's clinical development pipeline. The successful candidate will bring deep expertise in histology and tissue-based technologies, including immunohistochemistry, in situ hybridization, multiplex assays, and digital pathology. They will develop scientific talent and partner across our Company teams to deliver decision-enabling biomarker data for clinical programs. Primary Activities Scientific and Technical Leadership • Provide strategic and operational leadership for the development, validation, and clinical deployment of tissue-based biomarker assays. • Establish scientifically rigorous, fit-for-purpose assay strategies aligned with the biomarker question, stage of development, and intended use. • Advise on tissue acquisition and handling strategies and provide technical guidance on experiment design and assay validation for early- and late-stage clinical programs. • Evaluate and implement new technologies that expand Molecular Pathology capabilities and demonstrate value in translational biomarker development. People Leadership • Build, lead, mentor, and develop a high-performing team of scientists in an inclusive environment in which team members contribute their perspectives, challenge constructively, and deliver results together. • Set clear roles and performance expectations aligned with portfolio priorities while fostering accountability, scientific rigor, collaboration, and innovation. • Contribute to internal and external scientific communications, including study reports, publications, conference presentations, and capability presentations. Laboratory Operations, Quality, and Compliance • Provide daily laboratory leadership, including work prioritization, capacity planning, sample and reagent readiness, data review, instrument oversight, documentation, and timely delivery of high-quality results. • Manage laboratory resources, budgets, capital planning, and equipment lifecycles. • Establish robust processes for assay development, validation, transfer, clinical sample testing, reagent management, and equipment maintenance. • Ensure that laboratory activities are conducted in accordance with applicable safety requirements, standard operating procedures, quality standards, and regulatory expectations, including applicable GxP, CAP, or CLIA requirements. • Oversee the preparation, review, and approval of assay development and analytical validation plans and reports, standard operating procedures, and laboratory records • Provide technical oversight of external tissue assay vendors and partner laboratories, including vendor selection and qualification, quality review, performance monitoring, issue resolution, and delivery of fit-for-purpose assay results and documentation. Education Minimum Requirement • Master’s degree, Ph.D., M.D., or international equivalent professional degree in a life sciences discipline. Required Experience and Skills • 12+ years of experience with a Master’s degree or 10+ years with a Ph.D. or M.D., including at least three years of direct people management or laboratory leadership • Demonstrated ability to lead laboratory operations, balance multiple priorities, allocate resources, manage timelines, and deliver high-quality results on time. • Strong working knowledge of fit-for-purpose bioanalytical development and clinical laboratory quality systems, including GxP, CAP, and CLIA requirements where applicable. • Proven ability to influence, collaborate, and communicate complex scientific and operational topics clearly across functions. The MES Specialist’s primary responsibility is to support and help sustain that the deployment of our Company standard MES system is successfully and compliantly designed, developed, deployed, and supported to maximize business benefits and are in line with site business process and technical standards. The MES Specialist will have regular direct interaction with the Site Digital Steward, MBR authors, MES site organization, MES and SAP COE’s, Tech Ops, Operations, Quality, and IT. The Specialist is responsible for following standard processes and procedures in performing their duties. These include cGMP regulations, SOPs and global business processes. The MES Specialist is responsible for activities that include the following: Identifies and implements continuous process improvement opportunities. Coordinates and approves relevant procedures for MES access and user management, performance management, qualifications and testing, may participate in vulnerability assessments, IT hardware to include workstation design and setup on the production lines, business continuity planning, obsolescence planning and the main site contact for MES upgrades and continuous system improvements. Works with site and above site MES teams to sustain electronic Master Batch Records, stays relevant on MES training, coordinates site MES administration activities, knowledge of manufacturing processes, and standard MES configuration. Is liaison to MES COE, AMS and Digital Manufacturing organizations. Will be heavily involved in MES / MBR deployments at the site and assist in key project activities. Executes the appropriate change control and MES site life-cycle actions and processes to assure the MES system is in a state of control and compliance. Collaborates and assists with troubleshooting to efficiently resolve manufacturing problems, providing MES support to operations. Knowledge of Quality Systems and Regulatory Standards to provide assurance and foster quality decisions with project teams and their site Quality unit. Support other digital system initiatives such as OEE+ as needed. description: Job Description The Clinical Services Operations Coordinator, under the guidance of a West Point laboratory animal resources husbandry operations, works to provide world class animal care to impact drug development and discovery and improve human health. With minimal direction and in compliance with departmental Standard Operating Procedures, our Research & Development division study requirements, as well as applicable regulations and guidelines to include USDA regs, NIH Guide and, Good Laboratory Practices, this position oversees the details of animal care and related activities of Laboratory Animal Resources, to include indirect guidance of animal care workers. Has responsibility to assist with the training, development, assignment coordination and safety of hourly personnel. Contributes to making work assignments, ensuring completion and quality, and administers personnel policies. Ensures that quality support of research laboratory animal programs is a team effort between LAR, research staff and other support organizations. Collaborates across projects; communicates work related information to project teams: some contacts outside the department / company; may represent functional group on department teams or committees. Independently carries out minor technical duties related to laboratory practices, supplies organization, and laboratory records management. Contributions include: Contributes to interdepartmental collaborations with other members of our Research & Development division community. Assists with managerial reports as required (census, facility records) Communicates effectively, both verbal and written, with departmental and research staff. Assumes an assistant role in training of departmental staff in specific activities. Provides guidance to husbandry staff in conjunction with line management. Assists with the processing of orders of animals to meet research needs. In collaboration with other LAR personnel assists with the development and implementation of equipment and process validation programs. This includes but is not limited to, the validation of sanitation procedures, water testing, airborne particulate analysis, and temperature and light level testing and validation. Maintains animal source and transaction records in compliance with our Company, state and federal requirements. Assists with development, implementation, and monitoring of SOPs for daily activities. Manages husbandry equipment including rack washers, bottle washers, Tunnels washers, automated bedding systems and bulk sterilizers, and trains employees in their operation. Rooted in direct experience on the farm and in the clinic, we work hand in hand with our customers every step of the way. Our singular focus is to empower those who care for animals, helping them manage their vital responsibility with confidence. Because when it comes to animal health, no one sees it like we do. The Packaging Technician position is available at our Animal Health facility in De Soto, Kansas, located near Kansas City metropolitan area. The DeSoto facility is expanding operations to manufacturing vaccines and biologics for large and companion animals and leveraging an experienced and innovative team environment, the key technologies at the site are biologics production using fermentation and cell culture platforms, filling and packaging. Working within the packaging operations teams you will be expected to be able to work independently and as part of the team to contribute to the daily completion and schedule adherence of production activities. The packaging operation is made up of teams that carry out the day to day production activities of sealed bottle label application, bottle packaging, palletization, process document completion, cycle counting, and inventory reconciliation. The position requires someone who can demonstrate good attention to detail and achieve a consistent error-free execution of daily job responsibilities, be able to complete documentation using Good Documentation Practices and be able to identify opportunities for process improvement and employ basic problem-solving skills. title: Executive Director, Public Policy & Government Relations Animal Health Europe
description: Job Description We are searching for an Executive Director, Public Policy and Government Relations to join our team in Brussels with responsibility for for developing and executing public policy and government relations activities in line with the Europe animal health business. This position will report directly to the Associate Vice President of Global Animal Health Public Policy and Government Relations with a dotted line of reporting into the Senior Vice President for EURAM (Europe, Russia, Africa, Middle East) and will sit on the Leadership Teams of both Animal Health Global Public Policy & Government Relations and the EURAM Commercial regional leadership team (RLT). In addition to biopharma, this position will be responsible for overseeing the strategic development of the Technology intelligence product and solutions portfolio, which will include stakeholders outside of the animal health biopharma industry. This role will oversee the strategic engagement and execution of legislative and regulatory policies at the European Union institutional level . The issue areas will include but are not limited to animal health and welfare, food safety, trade, sustainability, traceability and monitoring and data policy. Primary Activities Partners with the EURAM leadership team and key stakeholders towards building successful business strategies. Lead a multi-faceted team that works at the EU Institutional level, within the Brussels-based Embassy community, as well as multi-lateral organizations such as the regional representatives at the World Organization for Animal Health (WOAH). Engage across the complex animal health eco-system with diverse customer and specie (cattle, swine, aqua, poultry, small animal, equine) strategies across bio-pharma and technology business approaches. Lead with a strategic and enterprise-wide mindset by collaborating with other business functions and regions of the business to develop and execute regional strategic priorities in line with enterprise wide business priorities. Position the business and advocate on issues related to digital, data and technology including stakeholder analysis, engagement, and management. Represent the company in trade associations such as AnimalhealthEurope (AHE), manage the relationships with key customer trade associations within the food/agriculture industry, companion animal, policy/trade associations and business groups. Reputation management as One Company including both human and animal health. Partner with other animal health policy regional and country leads and multi-lateral colleagues to develop global strategies for execution in Europe region to achieve a business objective or reputational need. description: Job Description Associate Director, Maintenance – Wilmington Biologics Site Position Summary The Associate Director, Maintenance provides strategic and operational leadership for the development, implementation, and execution of the maintenance program supporting the Wilmington biologics manufacturing campus. This role is accountable for ensuring that facility, utility, laboratory, warehouse, and manufacturing-support assets are maintained safely, reliably, compliantly, and efficiently to enable startup, qualification, commercial readiness, and sustained operations. Reporting to the Director of Engineering, Maintenance & Utilities (EMU), the Associate Director builds and leads the site maintenance organization, including maintenance leaders, planners and schedulers, skilled technicians, and supporting contractors. The role establishes the maintenance operating model, work-management processes, asset and preventive-maintenance data, spare-parts strategy, performance metrics, and governance required for a greenfield biologics facility. This leader partners closely with Engineering, Reliability, Facilities, Manufacturing, Quality, Validation, Automation, Metrology, EHSS, Supply Chain, Capital Projects, and Global Engineering to ensure an effective transition from design and construction through commissioning, qualification, startup, and routine GMP operations. Maintenance Leadership and Organizational Development Provide strategic leadership, technical direction, and coaching to the site maintenance organization supporting the Wilmington campus. Design, build, and scale the maintenance organization to meet phased facility startup and commercial manufacturing requirements. Lead maintenance first-line managers, planners and schedulers, mechanical and electrical technicians, instrumentation support, and contracted maintenance resources. Establish clear roles, decision rights, escalation pathways, shift coverage, and on-call support for safe and reliable operations. Build organizational capability through recruiting, onboarding, qualification, technical training, succession planning, and employee development. Greenfield Maintenance Program and Operational Readiness Develop and implement the site maintenance strategy, governance model, procedures, standards, and business processes for a new biologics manufacturing facility. Create the maintenance readiness plan aligned with building completion, equipment turnover, commissioning and qualification, engineering runs, process validation, and commercial startup. Ensure maintenance requirements are incorporated into equipment design reviews, maintainability assessments, vendor packages, FATs, SATs, commissioning activities, and operational handover. Establish asset acceptance criteria and verify that technical documentation, recommended spare parts, maintenance instructions, warranties, training, and vendor support are complete before ownership transfer. Coordinate phased deployment of maintenance staffing, tools, shops, service contracts, and support infrastructure as the campus becomes operational. Maintenance Operations and Work Management Own the site maintenance work-management process, including work identification, prioritization, planning, scheduling, execution, closeout, and performance review. Establish preventive, predictive, condition-based, corrective, emergency, and shutdown maintenance workflows consistent with cGMP and site procedures. Lead daily and weekly maintenance planning and scheduling routines in coordination with Manufacturing, Utilities Operations, Facilities, Quality, and Supply Chain. Ensure maintenance work is executed with appropriate job plans, permits, risk assessments, lockout/tagout controls, parts, tools, labor estimates, and quality documentation. Develop effective 24/7 response and escalation processes for critical equipment, utility, facility, and infrastructure failures. Drive schedule compliance, backlog health, wrench time, first-time quality, and timely closure of maintenance records. Asset Reliability and Lifecycle Management Partner with Reliability Engineering and system owners to develop asset criticality rankings, maintenance strategies, and lifecycle plans Implement reliability-centered maintenance, predictive maintenance, and condition-monitoring technologies based on equipment risk and failure modes. Lead or support equipment investigations, root-cause analyses, FMEAs, bad-actor elimination, and corrective and preventive actions. Use performance and failure data to optimize maintenance frequencies, job plans, spare-parts holdings, and asset replacement strategies. Ensure maintenance strategies support critical GMP utilities and infrastructure, including WFI, Purified Water, Clean Steam, process gases, HVAC, chilled water, steam, compressed air, electrical distribution, emergency power, UPS, refrigeration, and wastewater interfaces. Support reliable operation of manufacturing-support, laboratory, warehouse, and building systems across the Wilmington campus. CMMS, Maintenance Data, and Digital Systems Serve as the business owner for maintenance processes within the computerized maintenance management system (CMMS). Establish the asset hierarchy, equipment records, functional locations, maintenance plans, task lists, job plans, bills of materials, labor standards, and master-data governance required for startup. Ensure maintenance master data is accurate, complete, controlled, and aligned with engineering drawings, turnover packages, equipment tags, and the qualified state. Define user roles, workflows, reporting, and data-quality expectations for planners, supervisors, technicians, engineers, and contractors. Leverage digital tools, mobile execution, dashboards, and analytics to improve maintenance productivity, compliance, and equipment performance. Partner with Automation, IT, Engineering, and Reliability to integrate condition-monitoring and asset-performance information where appropriate. Spare Parts, Materials, and Vendor Management Develop and implement the site spare-parts and maintenance-materials strategy, including critical spares, insurance spares, consumables, repairables, and vendor-managed inventory. Establish spare-parts criticality, stocking levels, preservation requirements, storage conditions, cycle counting, obsolescence management, and replenishment processes. Ensure bills of materials and equipment-to-spare relationships are established in the CMMS and aligned with manufacturer recommendations and reliability risk. Partner with Supply Chain, Procurement, Engineering, and Logistics to establish storeroom operations and material availability for planned and emergency work. Develop and govern maintenance service contracts, vendor scopes, performance expectations, safety requirements, quality agreements where applicable, and service-level metrics. Manage original equipment manufacturer and specialty contractor support during startup and routine operations. Compliance and Inspection Readiness Ensure maintenance activities comply with cGMP, FDA, EMA, OSHA, EPA, company quality standards, site procedures, and applicable engineering codes. Maintain inspection readiness for maintenance records, preventive-maintenance execution, equipment history, work-order documentation, deviations, CAPAs, change controls, and contractor activities. Ensure maintenance is performed without compromising validated systems, product quality, data integrity, environmental controls, or the qualified state. Establish maintenance documentation standards and right-first-time expectations for work-order completion and technical records. Support internal audits, health authority inspections, quality reviews, and responses to maintenance-related observations. Partner with Quality, Validation, Metrology, and system owners to coordinate post-maintenance testing, calibration, return-to-service, and release requirements. Shutdowns, Startup Support, and Business Continuity Lead maintenance planning and execution for site shutdowns, turnarounds, utility outages, equipment interventions, and major preventive-maintenance campaigns. Develop integrated shutdown schedules, resource plans, contractor strategies, parts readiness, risk controls, and contingency plans. Coordinate maintenance support during commissioning, qualification, engineering runs, process validation, and startup activities. Establish emergency maintenance response and business-continuity plans for critical equipment and utility failures. Participate in site emergency response, incident command, and recovery activities as required. Conduct post-event reviews and implement lessons learned to improve future shutdown and outage performance. Capital Projects, CQV, and Operational Handover Represent Maintenance in capital project design reviews, constructability and maintainability assessments, equipment selection, and lifecycle-cost decisions. Provide maintenance input to user requirements, design specifications, equipment standards, access requirements, lifting and handling provisions, and serviceability expectations. Participate in FAT, SAT, commissioning, qualification, and startup activities to ensure equipment is maintainable and ready for operational ownership. Define and track maintenance deliverables within project turnover packages, including manuals, drawings, parts lists, training, warranties, job plans, and CMMS data. Ensure deficiencies affecting safe maintenance, reliability, or lifecycle support are resolved before final handover. Support capital planning for equipment replacement, reliability improvements, maintenance infrastructure, and lifecycle-risk reduction. Safety, Operational Excellence, and Performance Management Promote a strong safety culture and ensure maintenance work complies with lockout/tagout, electrical safety, confined-space, hot-work, line-break, work-at-height, and permit-to-work requirements. Lead continuous-improvement initiatives using Lean, problem-solving, and operational-excellence methodologies. Develop and manage maintenance KPIs, including safety, preventive-maintenance compliance, schedule compliance, backlog, downtime, mean time between failures, mean time to repair, work-order quality, labor productivity, and maintenance cost. Establish tiered performance reviews and visual-management routines to identify risks, prioritize actions, and sustain accountability. Develop and manage the maintenance operating budget, contractor spend, tooling requirements, and resource forecasts. Identify opportunities to improve asset reliability, reduce unplanned downtime, optimize maintenance costs, and increase workforce effectiveness. Cross-Functional Collaboration Partner with Manufacturing, Utilities Operations, Engineering, Reliability, Facilities, Automation, Validation, Metrology, Quality, EHSS, Supply Chain, Procurement, Capital Projects, Global Engineering, and external service providers. Coordinate maintenance priorities and equipment availability with production and utility operating plans. Build effective interfaces among maintenance, engineering system owners, reliability engineers, and operations teams. Communicate equipment risks, backlog constraints, shutdown needs, resource requirements, and recovery plans clearly to site leadership. Represent Maintenance in site governance forums, project reviews, readiness assessments, and operational performance meetings. People Leadership Lead, mentor, and develop a high-performing, diverse maintenance organization. Set clear performance expectations and promote accountability, collaboration, inclusion, and continuous learning. Develop technical qualification and progression pathways for maintenance supervisors, planners, schedulers, and technicians. Ensure contractors and contingent workers meet site expectations for safety, quality, technical competency, and performance. Create a culture of disciplined execution, problem solving, ownership, and reliable service to internal customers. Basic Qualifications Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Maintenance Management, or a related technical discipline. 10+ years of maintenance, engineering, reliability, or operations experience in pharmaceutical, biotechnology, medical device, or other regulated manufacturing. 5+ years of people-leadership experience within maintenance, engineering, or technical operations. Demonstrated experience leading maintenance work-management processes and multidisciplinary technical teams. Preferred Qualifications Experience developing or leading maintenance programs for a greenfield pharmaceutical or biologics manufacturing facility. Experience supporting commissioning, qualification, startup, process validation, and operational handover. Strong knowledge of CMMS implementation and master data, asset hierarchy, preventive-maintenance development, planning and scheduling, and spare-parts management. Experience with critical GMP utilities, central utility buildings, electrical distribution, HVAC, automation, and manufacturing-support systems. Knowledge of reliability-centered maintenance, predictive technologies, root-cause analysis, Lean, and operational-excellence tools. Experience managing maintenance contractors, service agreements, operating budgets, and shutdown execution. Knowledge of cGMP, data integrity, OSHA requirements, NFPA 70E, lockout/tagout, and applicable regulatory expectations. Core Competencies Strategic Maintenance Leadership Greenfield Operational Readiness Maintenance Work Management CMMS and Master Data Governance Planning and Scheduling Asset Reliability and Lifecycle Management Spare Parts and Materials Management GMP Compliance and Inspection Readiness Shutdown and Business Continuity Leadership Contractor and Vendor Management Operational Excellence and Performance Management People Development and Organizational Capability VETJOBS Required Skills: Analytical Thinking, Analytical Thinking, Asset Life Cycle Management, Contractor Management, Corrective Maintenance, Cross-Cultural Awareness, Deviation Management, Engineering Principle, Engineering Standards, Environmental Safety, Equipment Maintenance, Lockout Tagout, Maintenance Audits, Maintenance Coordination, Maintenance Management, Maintenance Scheduling, Maintenance Supervision, Manufacturing Quality Control, Manufacturing Scale-Up, Multi Disciplinary Design, Operational Excellence, Operational Safety, Operation Maintenance, Parts Inventory, Parts Sourcing {+ 8 more} Preferred Skills: Current Employees apply HERE Current Contingent Workers apply HERE US and Puerto Rico Residents Only: Our company is committed to inclusion, ensuring that candidates can engage in a hiring process that exhibits their true capabilities. title: Regional Director – Vaccines & Infectious Disease
description: Job Description Join us at a pivotal time of innovation, growth, and breakthrough launches. Create lasting impact by connecting global vision with local execution and lead the Vaccines & Infectious Diseases franchise across Asia Pacific to shape the future of healthcare. Drive strategy, launches, and growth across one of the world's most dynamic regions. Bring life-changing innovation to millions of patients. Our Human Health Division maintains a “patient first, profits later” ideology. The organization is comprised of sales, marketing, market access, digital analytics and commercial professionals who are passionate about their role in bringing our medicines to our customers worldwide. Role Overview The Regional Franchise Director is the regional commercial owner and ambassador for the Vaccines & Infectious Diseases Franchise across Asia Pacific. The role is responsible for shaping franchise strategy, brand planning, portfolio prioritization, forecasting, and lifecycle strategy across while driving strong cross‑functional execution to deliver business results. Operating as a regional commercial leader, the Regional Franchise Director is a trusted commercial partner to markets, global teams, and regional leadership—bringing clarity, discipline, and momentum to strategy, launch readiness, and ongoing performance. The role requires strong strategic thinking, business judgment, analytical discipline, and cross-functional leadership. Together with the regional marketing team, the Regional Franchise Director will translate market insights, competitive intelligence, access realities, customer needs, and financial assumptions into clear strategic recommendations, actionable brand plans, and high-quality business decisions across Asia Pacific. What will you do in this role Franchise / Brand Strategy & Ownership Own and articulate the regional strategy for the assigned franchise/brand/asset, aligned to global direction and adapted for AP market realities. Serve as the regional ambassador and subject‑matter expert, providing clear strategic direction to markets. Define what is standard vs. localized across messaging, campaigns, and execution. Own the brand narrative and storytelling, translating strategy into clear, executable plans. Regional–Global–Local Orchestration Act as the primary connector between global, regional, and local teams for the franchise/asset. Adapt global strategies and campaigns to ensure local relevance without strategic dilution. Ensure markets understand not just what to do, but why —making strategy practical and actionable. Cross‑Functional Leadership & Execution Mobilise and align cross‑functional teams (marketing, sales, access, medical, finance, policy, etc.). Drive executional excellence across launch preparation, brand activation, and lifecycle management. Navigate competing priorities while maintaining focus, alignment, and momentum. Market & Stakeholder Partnership Be a high‑value partner to markets, enabling MDs, BU Heads, and local teams through clarity and support. Partner closely with marketing, sales, and access colleagues to drive brand and business performance. Build trust as a commercial thought partner, not a service provider. Commercial Leadership Demonstrate commercial and P&L awareness for the Franchise/asset. Partner with Business Unit Directors and escalate to MDs when appropriate and value‑adding. Solve problems pragmatically, balancing strategic intent with execution realities. People Leadership and Capability Building Guide, coach, and support marketers or project teams responsible for assigned brand and indication priorities. Create clarity on priorities, deliverables, timelines, decision points, and ways of working to ensure strong strategic discipline and accountability. Build marketing capability across strategic planning, brand planning, forecasting, opportunity assessment, competitive strategy, and cross-functional leadership. Contribute to a collaborative, accountable, and inclusive team culture that enables high performance across regional and country teams. What should you have: Required Hands on experience in Vaccines and Infectious Diseases franchise leadership within a regional or matrixed environment. Proven ability to develop strategy and translate it into execution. Strong grounding in marketing excellence and structured marketing capabilities. Demonstrated cross‑functional leadership and stakeholder management skills. Excellent storytelling and executive communication capability. Curiosity and ability to apply AI in analysis, communication and execution Preferred Asia Pacific market experience. Exposure to launch planning and lifecycle management. Comfort operating with senior stakeholders at regional and global levels. Who We Are: We are known as Merck & Co., Inc., Rahway, New Jersey, USA in the United States and Canada, and MSD everywhere else. For more than a century, we have been bringing forward medicines and vaccines for many of the world’s most challenging diseases. Today, we continue to advance innovative health solutions that improve and save lives around the world. What We Look For: Imagine starting each day knowing your work helps save and improve lives. Supports the implementation of microbiological methods (compendial/alternative microbiological methods) in a harmonized way to secure efficient implementation at the receiving unit (internally and/or externally). Provides scientific and practical support to analytical investigation during method suitability and routine use. Provides practical support for microbiological tests on an as-needed basis for methods and studies in their expertise for the transfer and commercialization of Biologicals/Vaccines. Participates as a SME in the evaluation, method development, method validation of alternative microbiological technology (Rapid Microbiology Methods). Responsible for authoring primary and secondary source documents used for regulatory filings. Project Member and/or lead. Support the implementation of microbiological methods at receiving units. Supports as SME the Dunboyne QC-Micro and AS&T team. Participates in Root Cause Analysis as SME for significant investigations. Participates as SME in multidisciplinary teams solving technical problems at global or multisite level. Participates in global change control processes as an SME or as change owner. Takes GMP requirements into account when setting up experiments and protocols. Ensures compliance of protocols, lab data and reports. Ensures safety at personnel and at lab level. Join an innovative team at one of the largest pharmaceutical manufacturing companies in the Netherlands. At our Haarlem site, we have an exciting opportunity for a Medical Device & Combination Product (MDCP) Engineer . Welcome to our team Are you ready to make a global impact in medical device development? As a MDCP Engineer in Device Development & Technology (DD&T), you will drive innovative medical devices and combination products through development, qualification, commercialization, and long-term sustainment. Working in a highly collaborative environment, you will partner with Manufacturing, Quality, Operations, Product Development, Regulatory Affairs, Procurement, and external suppliers to drive innovation, technical excellence, and continuous improvement across a global product portfolio. Purpose of the role As a Medical Device & Combination Product (MDCP) Engineer , you will support the development, technology transfer, commercialization, and lifecycle management of medical devices and combination products, with a particular focus on autoinjectors, pre-filled syringes, and co-packed products. You will apply your expertise in design controls, device risk management, process development, process validation, and automation to solve complex technical challenges and support compliant manufacturing operations. This role requires strong problem-solving skills, the ability to manage competing priorities, and effective communication with a broad range of stakeholders. You will work independently on defined projects while collaborating with global and site-based teams to drive investigations, process improvements, and strategic initiatives. Key stakeholders include packaging technology teams, quality organizations, manufacturing operations, product development, regulatory affairs, procurement, and external suppliers. Tasks and responsibilities Facilitate technology and design transfer of medical devices and combination products from development through commercialization. Contribute to the design, build, and validation of semi-automated and fully automated autoinjector assembly systems and combination product kit assembly lines. Own the technical aspects of investigations related to the qualification and commercial operation of MDCP assembly systems. Support root cause analyses, CAPA activities, deviation investigations, and troubleshooting efforts. Utilize device risk management tools (d/pFMEA, QRA, OER, etc.) to support the development and maintenance of device and combination product risk management files. Demonstrate strong communication skills by integrating input from multiple stakeholders and effectively communicating decisions to key stakeholders and sponsors. Actively seek feedback to ensure customer and stakeholder needs remain central to decision-making and expectations. What we ask BS degree or higher in Engineering (Mechanical, Biomedical, Chemical, Materials, or similar). 3+ years of experience in medical devices or combination products (e.g., autoinjectors, pre-filled syringes, MDCPs). Experience with manufacturing equipment, automation, DFM, and qualification activities (IQ/OQ/PQ). Knowledge of root cause analysis, structured problem-solving, and process improvement. Experience with design transfer, tech transfer, process validation, and scale-up. Strong understanding of risk management (FMEA, hazard analysis, control strategies). Experience with change control, deviation management, and QMS documentation. Cross-functional project management experience in international environments. Excellent communication skills in English; Dutch is a plus. Join a team that is passionate about using data, analytics, and insights to drive decision-making and create custom software, allowing us to tackle some of the world's greatest health threats. Our Technology Centres focus on creating a space where teams can come together to deliver business solutions that save and improve lives. An integral part of our company's IT operating model, Tech Centres are globally distributed locations where each IT division has employees to enable our digital transformation journey and drive business outcomes. title: Associate Principal Scientist
description: Job Description Associate Principal Scientist, Process Chemistry The Process Chemistry organization, located at our Rahway, NJ site, is seeking a highly motivated and accomplished scientist with deep expertise in flow chemistry and continuous processing to join the Catalysis and Flow Lab. This position offers an opportunity to play a key role in advancing our pipeline of drug substances, including small molecules, macrocyclic peptides, and bioconjugates, by developing and implementing robust, sustainable, and efficient API manufacturing processes from discovery through commercialization. The successful candidate will lead laboratory experimentation in flow chemistry, develop and implement novel continuous processing technologies, enable new chemical transformations, and influence route design across development programs. The role requires close collaboration with multidisciplinary teams, including synthetic and analytical chemists, chemical engineers, manufacturing partners, and other stakeholders, to support API campaigns at laboratory, pilot, and manufacturing scales. Responsibilities also include solving complex chemistry and processing challenges, supporting technology transfer, mentoring scientists new to the field, and contributing to the external scientific community through publications, patents, presentations, and professional engagement. The ideal candidate will possess strong expertise in synthetic organic chemistry, process development, flow chemistry, and continuous processing, along with the passion and capability to serve as a subject matter expert within the Process Chemistry Department. A proven record of scientific innovation, technical achievement, self-initiative, and effective collaboration in a dynamic team environment is essential. Specific Responsibilities Provide scientific leadership for the design, development, and optimization of scalable API processes across multiple development programs, with a strong emphasis on flow chemistry and continuous processing. Lead hands-on laboratory experimentation in flow chemistry to develop robust, sustainable, and efficient chemical transformations and manufacturing processes. Influence route design and solve complex chemistry, engineering, and manufacturing challenges through mechanistic understanding, innovative process design, and data-driven decision-making. Support process characterization, scale-up, technology transfer, and API campaigns at laboratory, pilot, and manufacturing scales in collaboration with cross-functional partners. Mentor scientists and colleagues new to flow chemistry and continuous processing while fostering a culture of scientific excellence, innovation, and collaboration. Contribute to the broader scientific community through publications, patents, presentations, and professional engagement. Education Minimum Requirement Ph.D. in Chemistry or a related discipline. Required Experience and Skills Minimum of 4 years of relevant industrial experience following completion of a Ph.D., with demonstrated success in small-molecule process chemistry using flow chemistry. Strong experience in organic synthesis, flow chemistry, and continuous processing, including hands-on laboratory experimentation in flow. Proven ability to design, develop, and optimize practical, scalable chemical processes through scientific rigor, creativity, and data-driven problem-solving. Ability to apply flow chemistry and continuous processing technologies to enable new chemical transformations, influence route design, and address complex process development challenges. Experience with automation approaches for continuous-flow process development is highly valued. Demonstrated success working across multidisciplinary teams and effectively communicating technical concepts to scientific and non-scientific audiences. Strong written communication skills, with the ability to prepare clear technical reports, presentations, publications, and documentation. Strong self-initiative, collaborative mindset, and enthusiasm for serving as a subject matter expert in flow chemistry while mentoring others new to the field. Demonstrated scientific impact through publications, patents, presentations, or participation in the broader scientific community. The maintenance scheduler role is predominantly forward-looking and seldom becomes involved in work execution. The scheduler will work collaboratively with all stakeholders, drive work prioritization, and engage the proper resources to create maintenance schedules for all planned Preventative, Predictive and Corrective work orders, that can be executed right first time. The scheduler actively ensures GMP quality, safety, environmental, and operating cost goals are achieved, and may sometimes provide supervisory coverage of hourly mechanic workforce to ensure supply of a high quality product. description: Job Description Role Overview This role is part of a broader enterprise initiative to establish a Data Context Layer (DCL) — a foundational capability designed to provide consistent, reusable, and scalable context across enterprise data products. The DCL is intended to address challenges related to data fragmentation, lack of shared semantics, and inconsistent interpretation of data across systems and products . It establishes a unified layer for representing context, relationships, and meaning, enabling downstream products to operate with greater consistency, interoperability, and intelligence. In addition, the DCL plays a critical role in enabling agentic AI capabilities across the enterprise by providing the structured context and semantic grounding required for intelligent agents to operate reliably. This includes ensuring that agent-driven workflows and decisions are based on consistent, governed, and interpretable data context , reducing risks associated with fragmentation, ambiguity, and lack of control. Within this initiative, we are seeking a UX/Service Designer to design the end-to-end experience for an enterprise capability that enables teams to publish, discover, and consume standardized data context through self-service . This role will focus on defining user journeys, service blueprints, interaction models, prototype user interfaces, and operating processes that make the platform usable, trustworthy, and scalable across the enterprise. The ideal candidate has strong service design skills, experience working with technical platforms, and the ability to translate complex data/semantic/AI concepts into intuitive user experiences. title: Instructional Designer/Developer
description: Job Description Position Overview The Learning & Development Designer/Developer is responsible for the end-to-end design and development of learning products and solutions within Global Learning & Development’s Regional Capability Center. Reporting to the Production Team Leader, this role combines instructional design and hands-on development responsibilities, enabling flexible, high quality, and efficient learning production at scale. The Designer/Developer partners with project managers, localization leads, subject matter experts, and GLD stakeholders to deliver learner-centric, outcomes focused learning experiences aligned to GLD standards. The Learning & Development Designer/Developer is responsible for: Learning Design & Solution Development Design and develop learning solutions across modalities (e.g., digital learning, virtual, blended, performance support) based on defined learning objectives, success criteria, and GLD standards. Translate business requirements, learning blueprints, and high-level designs into detailed instructional designs and completed learning assets. Apply adult learning principles, learning science, and GLD’s learning model to create effective, engaging, and inclusive learning experiences. Hands‑On Content Development Build learning assets using approved authoring tools, templates, and platforms, ensuring consistency, reusability, and accessibility. Develop assessments, knowledge checks, and measurement approaches aligned to learning objectives. Incorporate feedback from reviews and quality checks to continuously improve deliverables. Collaboration & Delivery Execution Partner closely with Project Managers to support accurate scoping, timelines, and delivery commitments. Collaborate with SMEs, localization leads, and reviewers to ensure content accuracy, clarity, and readiness for localization or deployment. Support iterative development approaches, including Agile or rapid development models, to meet delivery timelines. Quality, Standards & Continuous Improvement Ensure all learning products meet GLD quality standards, brand guidelines, accessibility requirements, and compliance expectations. Leverage standardized processes, tools, and templates to drive efficiency and consistency. Identify opportunities to improve development efficiency, reuse content, and reduce cycle time. Ideally you should have: Bachelor’s degree in Instructional Design, Education, Learning Technology, Business, or a related field. 6+ years of experience in learning design and/or learning development, with demonstrated ability to perform both disciplines. Strong understanding of instructional design methodologies, adult learning principles, and learning experience design. Proven experience developing learning content using industry‑standard authoring tools and learning platforms. Ability to work effectively in high volume, production oriented environments with shifting priorities. Strong collaboration and communication skills, with experience working in cross functional and global teams. Attention to detail, strong organizational skills, and a commitment to quality and continuous improvement. Experience supporting localization, accessibility, and global deployment preferred.
